symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of labelled experimental units.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: \(t=(t_1,t_2,t_3)\) records one unit's three potential outcomes.

symbols.name: \mathcal T
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T=\{0,1\}^3\), containing the eight arm-labelled binary response types.

symbols.name: z
symbols.def: \(z=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) fixes all three potential outcomes of every labelled unit before assignment.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau
symbols.def: An arbitrary measurable, possibly biased decision rule clipped to the target range.

symbols.name: R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)
symbols.def: \(R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)=\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z))^2]\), with expectation only over \(A\).

symbols.name: q_n
symbols.def: The allocation vector used at population size \(n\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_q
symbols.def: Under \(\mathcal D_q\), the coordinates \(A_i\) are independent and \(\Pr(A_i=a)=q_a\).

symbols.name: \pi
symbols.def: \(\pi_r\) is the probability assigned to the uniform labelled assignment orbit with arm counts \(r\).

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: \(\delta(r,x)\) is the reported contrast after observing the allocation and success counts.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: \(h=(h_{t,a})\) records how many response-type \(t\) units are assigned to arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \mathcal H(m,r,x)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal H(m,r,x)\) contains all \(h\) with row sums \(m_t\), column sums \(r_a\), and \(\sum_{t:t_a=1}h_{t,a}=x_a\) for every \(a\).

symbols.name: P_m(x\mid r)
symbols.def: The probability of \(x\) under uniform labelled assignment conditional on arm counts \(r\) and schedule orbit \(m\).

symbols.name: G_n^{\mathrm{all}}
symbols.def: The minimax value of the eight-type orbit game when the designer chooses a distribution over \(r\).

symbols.name: G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)
symbols.def: The eight-type orbit-game value with the multinomial law of \(r\) induced by \(\mathcal D_q\).

symbols.name: \lambda
symbols.def: \(\lambda=(\lambda_t)\) is the \(n^{2/3}\)-scale intensity of the six response types off the edge spanned by \(000\) and \(111\).

symbols.name: \phi_3
symbols.def: \(\phi_3\) is the positive multiple of \(u\mapsto\operatorname{Ai}(|u|/2-C_3)\) normalized by \(\int\phi_3^2=1\).

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: A scalar local mean parameter used to generate complete schedules before assignment.

symbols.name: f
symbols.def: A smooth compactly supported approximation to \(\phi_3^2\).

symbols.name: \Pi_{A,n}
symbols.def: The label-preserving local prior constructed from \(\alpha=n^{-1/3}X\) and the four half-effect response types.

symbols.name: V_a
symbols.def: The \(V_a\) are independent with density \(15(1-v^2)^2/16\) on \([-1,1]\).

symbols.name: U_i
symbols.def: The \(U_i\) are independent uniform variables and are independent of the arm perturbations.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: The reciprocal mesh scale for rational action discretization.

symbols.name: \Lambda_{n,M}^{\mathrm{all}}
symbols.def: The exact rational eight-type orbit-game value when actions are restricted to \(\Gamma_M\).

symbols.name: \Lambda_{n,M}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)
symbols.def: The corresponding exact rational value under the multinomial allocation law induced by \(q\).

assumptions.condition: The complete binary schedule \(z\) is fixed; probability statements condition on it.
The assignment law \(\mathcal D\) is selected without observing \(z\).

standard.name: Known randomized assignment independent of fixed potential outcomes

definitions.name: Unrestricted three-arm minimax game
definitions.construction: \[\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}=\inf_{\mathcal D\in\Delta(\mathcal A^n),\,\widehat\tau:\mathcal O_n\to[-1,1]}\max_{z\in\mathcal T^n}\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z)\}^2.\]

definitions.name: Finite orbit-game constructions
definitions.construction: Let \(\pi\) range over laws on arm-count vectors \(r\) with \(\sum_ar_a=n\), and let \(\delta(r,x)\in[-1,1]\). Define \(G_n^{\mathrm{all}}=\inf_{\pi,\delta}\max_{m\in\mathcal M_n}\sum_r\pi_r\sum_xP_m(x\mid r)\{\delta(r,x)-n^{-1}\sum_tm_t\mu(t)\}^2\). Define \(G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)\) by fixing \(\pi_r=n!\prod_aq_a^{r_a}/\prod_ar_a!\).

definitions.name: Stratified face/corner spectral experiment
definitions.construction: For each fixed \(\eta\), minimize \(\mathcal E_\eta(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\{4|\psi'(u)|^2+V(u,\eta)|\psi(u)|^2\}\,du\) over \(\psi\in H^1(\mathbb R)\) with \(\int\psi^2=1\). The full value is the infimum over fibers \(\eta\in\mathbb R\); the transverse dual is allowed to be a probability measure, including a point mass at \(\eta=0\).

definitions.name: Iid Airy-feedback procedure
definitions.construction: Under \(\mathcal D_q\), compute \(T_{n,q}=n^{-1}\sum_i c_{A_i}(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1/2)/q_{A_i}\) and report \(\delta_{n,q}=\operatorname{proj}_{[-1,1]}\{T_{n,q}-n^{-2/3}s_3(n^{1/3}T_{n,q})\}\), where \(s_3=-2\phi_3'/\phi_3\).

definitions.name: Label-preserving half-effect schedule prior
definitions.construction: Draw \(X\) with density \(f\), set \(\alpha=n^{-1/3}X\), and condition on \(|\alpha|<1/3\). Independently across labelled units draw response types according to \(p_t(\alpha)\). The induced law on complete schedules is \(\Pi_{A,n}\).

definitions.name: Allocation-regularized complete-schedule prior
definitions.construction: Draw \(V_a\) and \(U_i\) as specified, set \(P_a=1/2+\varepsilon_nV_a\), and form \(Y_i(a)=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le P_a\}\); the induced complete-schedule law is \(\Pi_{B,n}\). Define \(\Pi_n=(1-n^{-1/4})\Pi_{A,n}+n^{-1/4}\Pi_{B,n}\).

definitions.name: Exact rational finite-orbit certificate
definitions.construction: Restrict each orbit decision \(\delta(r,x)\) to a mixture over \(\Gamma_M\), linearize the resulting squared risks with nonnegative joint design--action weights, and minimize their common upper bound over the design-orbit law for \(\Lambda_{n,M}^{\mathrm{all}}\), or fix the multinomial \(q\)-law for \(\Lambda_{n,M}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)\).

definitions.name: Singular finite-orbit bridge handle
definitions.construction: Start from the exact likelihood \(P_m(x\mid r)\); stratify local type counts by \((\theta,\eta)\); use a discrete Stein expansion only in the target coordinate; retain zero-likelihood cells through the primal risk inequalities; compactify duals as probability measures in \(\eta\) with fiberwise \(H^1\) control in \(\theta\); and construct liminf and recovery comparisons uniform on shrinking neighborhoods of \(\eta=0\).

statements.statement: Import the lossless exact labelled eight-type orbit-game reduction established in the accepted repository parent \(\texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier}\). For every \(n\), common permutation symmetrization identifies \[\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}=G_n^{\mathrm{all}},\qquad \rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)=G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q).\] Its exact likelihood is \(P_m(x\mid r)\), and its attained finite primal and dual games retain zero arm counts and zero-likelihood observation cells.
statements.justification: This imported proposition is infrastructure only: it fixes the exact labelled finite experiment on which the new asymptotic claims are built.
statements.gap: No novelty is claimed for the orbit equality; the accepted repository parent supplies it, while the unresolved step is its uniform second-order analysis at the singular face/corner fiber.
statements.consumer: The imported finite experiment is the common starting point for the Airy constant, the singular bridge, and the allocation-frontier claims.

statements.statement: The six response types outside \(\{000,111\}\) have \((\mu(t),\nu(t),\mu(t)^2)\) equal to \((-1/2,-1,1/4)\), \((-1/2,1,1/4)\), \((-1,0,1)\), \((1,0,1)\), \((1/2,-1,1/4)\), and \((1/2,1,1/4)\). Consequently the tangent program has the exact value \[V(\theta,\eta)=\max\{|\theta|/2,|\eta|/4\}.\] Integer response-type counts recover every compact set of local coordinates with \(O(n^{-2/3})\) coordinate and cost error.
statements.justification: The polyhedral potential is the first mathematical step that differs from the published scalar two-arm boundary.
statements.gap: The two-arm potential in Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Section 3) is \(|\theta|\); no cited work derives this labelled face/corner support function.
statements.consumer: The explicit potential identifies which complete schedules drive second-order risk and makes the proposed constant numerically and analytically evaluable.

statements.statement: Under \(\Pi_{A,n}\), conditional on \(\alpha\) and any assignment vector, the signed observations \(\operatorname{sign}(c_{A_i})(2Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1)\) are independent with success probability \((1+\alpha)/2\), while the posterior mean of \(\tau(z)\) retains the arm-labelled coefficient \(b_{A_i}(\alpha)\). For \(\alpha=n^{-1/3}u\), the generalized information inequality and conditional-residual term give, uniformly over every schedule-independent \(\mathcal D\), the second-order coefficient \[I(f)+\{2\bar q_1(\mathcal D)-1/2\}m_1(f),\] up to \(o(1)\). The cusp at \(\alpha=0\) has cancelling traces and creates no extra boundary term.
statements.justification: This coefficient is the early kill test: omitting the label-dependent posterior target or its residual variance changes the proposed potential and constant.
statements.gap: The published two-arm lower bound uses a scalar target and symmetric least-favorable prior; it has no arm-labelled posterior coefficient or allocation-sensitive residual term.
statements.consumer: The exact coefficient supplies a trustworthy lower-bound diagnostic before the singular experiment-convergence argument is attempted.

statements.statement: The stratified face/corner experiment has value \[\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\inf_{\psi\in H^1(\mathbb R):\int\psi^2=1}\mathcal E_\eta(\psi)=\inf_{\psi:\int\psi^2=1}\int_{\mathbb R}\{4|\psi'(u)|^2+|u||\psi(u)|^2/2\}\,du=C_3.\] The least fiber is \(\eta=0\); \(\phi_3\) is its positive even ground state, satisfies \(\phi_3'(0)=0\), and has eigenvalue \(C_3=-a_1'\). Along the full integer sequence, the imported exact orbit games obey \[\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}=\frac1n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),\qquad \rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q^\star)=\frac1n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).\] Thus iid \(q^\star\) is second-order minimax and \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q^\star)-\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}=o(n^{-4/3})\). The new assertion is the exact half-wedge constant and its uniform transfer through the singular labelled finite experiment; the orbit equality itself is inherited infrastructure.
statements.justification: The theorem identifies the exact nonlinear gain from joint design and analysis and proves that a simple iid allocation attains the unrestricted benchmark to second order.
statements.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix C) provide the one-dimensional Airy method, but their scalar lattice argument does not determine the three-arm half-wedge eigenvalue \(-a_1'\) or justify transfer through the coalesced transverse fiber.
statements.consumer: For an active treatment compared with the equally weighted average of two binary comparators, the result supplies the sharp worst-case MSE benchmark and the exact magnitude of nonlinear improvement.

statements.statement: Let \((q_n)\) be iid allocation vectors with \(q_n\to q^\star\). Uniformly whenever \(\zeta_n=n^{1/6}(q_n-q^\star)\) ranges over a compact subset of \(\{v:v_1+v_2+v_3=0\}\), \[\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)=\frac1n+n^{-4/3}\{\mathsf P(\zeta_n)-C_3\}+o(n^{-4/3}).\] Hence an iid allocation array retains the unrestricted sharp correction \(C_3\) if and only if \(n^{1/6}(q_n-q^\star)\to0\). If \(q_n\to q^\star\) and \(n^{1/6}\|q_n-q^\star\|\to\infty\), then \(n^{4/3}\{\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)-n^{-1}\}\to\infty\). The penalty \(\mathsf P(\zeta)=2\zeta_1^2+4\zeta_2^2+4\zeta_3^2\) is the constrained Hessian of \(q\mapsto\frac14\sum_ac_a^2/q_a\), and the displayed expansion proves its uniform coupling to the half-wedge experiment.
statements.justification: This necessary-and-sufficient frontier turns the design into a first-class object and quantifies exactly when allocation error erases the second-order minimax gain.
statements.gap: Bai (2023, Theorems 3.1--3.3) gives a first-order quadratic allocation result for linear procedures, while Zhao and Ding (2023) hold limiting multi-arm proportions fixed; neither derives the \(n^{-1/6}\) threshold or couples it to nonlinear minimax risk.
statements.consumer: A multi-arm trial can translate the theorem into an allocation-tolerance rule: deviations smaller than \(n^{-1/6}\) preserve the sharp gain, while local deviations incur the explicit penalty.

statements.statement: At \(q=q^\star\), the explicit estimator \(\delta_{n,q^\star}\) satisfies \[\max_{z\in\mathcal T^n}R_n(\mathcal D_{q^\star},\delta_{n,q^\star};z)\le n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\] uniformly over complete schedules. The explicit prior \(\Pi_n\) satisfies, uniformly over every schedule-independent \(\mathcal D\), \[\inf_{\widehat\tau}\mathbb E_{z\sim\Pi_n}R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)\ge n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).\] The broad component yields a positive quadratic coercivity term in \(\|\bar q(\mathcal D)-q^\star\|\); completing the square against the linear half-effect-prior term contributes only \(o(n^{-4/3})\). Finally, with \(M=n\), both rational grid programs bracket their continuous orbit games within \(1/(4n^2)=o(n^{-4/3})\).
statements.justification: The proposition makes the asymptotic saddle operational and prevents the sharp value from resting on an unattained formal operator.
statements.gap: The two-arm paper constructs a scalar feedback rule and scalar Airy-squared priors; the proposed constructions must preserve arm labels and regularize every dependent assignment law without changing the second-order coefficient.
statements.consumer: The estimator is directly implementable under iid \(q^\star\), while the rational certificates allow exact finite-sample auditing of its worst-case risk.

statements.statement: On the restricted schedule class \(Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\) for every \(i\), pool assignment labels \(2\) and \(3\). Under \(q^\star\), the resulting observation has balanced two-arm assignment, the target becomes \(n^{-1}\sum_i\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(2)\}\), and the exact orbit likelihood reduces to the shifted-binomial experiment of Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorem 2.1). Its restricted-class second-order constant is \(-4^{1/3}a_1'\), providing the required two-arm sanity reduction without asserting that this restricted constant equals \(C_3\).
statements.justification: The reduction verifies the normalization and distinguishes the new worst-case three-arm geometry from an embedded two-arm submodel.
statements.gap: The published scalar experiment supplies the known special case but does not establish how the unrestricted eight-type adversary lowers the constant to \(C_3\).
statements.consumer: The identity provides a regression test for symbolic and numerical implementations of the eight-type likelihood.

statements.statement: Can one construct a uniform liminf and recovery comparison between the exact eight-type orbit games and the stratified face/corner experiment, with risk error \(o(n^{-4/3})\), simultaneously for \(|\eta|\le\epsilon_n^{\mathrm{bridge}}\), the coalesced fiber \(\eta=0\), every mixture on the \(000\)--\(111\) nuisance edge, every zero-likelihood observation cell, and every dormant finite-game primal constraint? The comparison must justify measure-valued concentration on \(\eta=0\), continuity of the fiber wavefunction and its \(\theta\)-derivative at \(\theta=\pm|\eta|/2\), and absence of an artificial \(\eta\)-diffusion or \(\eta\)-boundary condition.
statements.justification: This is the genuine unresolved proof boundary separating a compelling formal constant from a theorem valid for the full labelled finite experiment.
statements.gap: Appendix C of Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) controls a one-dimensional lattice, while the prior orbit proposal permits arbitrary versions on null cells; neither result supplies uniform singular-fiber recovery.
statements.consumer: Closing the bridge validates the sharp constant, the allocation frontier, and the finite certificates simultaneously; failure pinpoints the first labelled orbit that requires a different limit experiment.

sampling_model.design: The unrestricted benchmark ranges over every law on \(\mathcal A^n\) chosen independently of the complete schedule; the attaining design is iid \(q^\star\), and the allocation frontier ranges over iid triangular arrays \(q_n\).
sampling_model.units: There are \(n\) labelled units with a fixed complete binary schedule \(z\in\{0,1\}^{3n}\); no superpopulation sampling is invoked.
sampling_model.treatment: Each unit receives exactly one of three labelled arms and reveals \(Y_i(A_i)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No positivity restriction is imposed on unrestricted competing designs; each iid frontier array is eventually in the interior because it converges to \(q^\star\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no estimated nuisance regressions. The nonlinear correction uses only the known allocation and the observed centered contrast score; all probability is assignment probability conditional on \(z\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For two-arm binary finite-population effects, unrestricted minimax risk is \(n^{-1}-(-4^{1/3}a_1')n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) and balanced Bernoulli assignment with nonlinear shrinkage attains it.
For two bounded-outcome arms, iid half assignment and a nonlinear endpoint-derived estimator attain the unrestricted minimax value characterized by a finite convex program.
Under the paper's permutation-invariant uncertainty class and linear-estimation formulation, complete randomization and a Neyman allocation solve the stated minimax problem.
For general multi-treatment finite-population contrasts and assignment mechanisms, the paper gives exact variance identities for linear unbiased estimators.
For multi-arm complete randomization with fixed limiting allocation proportions, regression-adjusted estimators admit regular design-based asymptotic comparisons.
Second-order asymptotic minimax behavior can be characterized by square completion and a problem-specific differential operator.
Restricted normal-mean minimax risk has a boundary-layer analysis based on least-favorable distributions.
Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population total estimation, pairwise-independent sampling and midpoint-differenced Horvitz--Thompson estimation attain the sharp minimax criterion.

tldr: For the binary three-arm contrast \((1,-1/2,-1/2)\), start from the lossless exact labelled eight-type orbit game imported from the accepted repository parent. The new field-level kernel identifies the half-wedge Airy constant \(C_3=-a_1'\), transfers it uniformly through the singular \(\eta=0\) fiber while retaining null observation cells and dormant primal constraints, and derives the sharp \(n^{-1/6}\) iid allocation frontier with penalty \(2\zeta_1^2+4\zeta_2^2+4\zeta_3^2\). The resulting unrestricted and iid \(q^\star=(1/2,1/4,1/4)\) risks share the expansion \(n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), supported by an Airy-feedback rule and a label-preserving, allocation-regularized complete-schedule prior.

project_justification.gap: The accepted repository parent settles the lossless exact multi-arm orbit reduction, but it does not identify the second-order constant, control the singular transverse fiber, or characterize allocation perturbations at the scale where first-order design loss meets nonlinear minimax gain.
project_justification.niche: For the symmetric active-arm-versus-pooled-comparators contrast, the inherited orbit game has an explicitly solvable half-wedge tangent geometry but a nonregular \(\eta=0\) bridge that is absent from scalar two-arm theory.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact half-wedge Airy constant, proves a uniform finite-orbit bridge with null-cell and dormant-constraint control, constructs matching upper and lower procedures, and establishes the necessary-and-sufficient \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation frontier.

related_work: The accepted repository parent \(\texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier}\) supplies the lossless labelled eight-type orbit-game reduction used here as infrastructure. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorems 2.2 and 3.1 and Appendix C) inform the one-dimensional score correction, Airy prior, and lattice comparison, but do not resolve the half-wedge constant or the singular transverse bridge. Hull (2026, Theorem 1 and proof A.4) informs the endpoint-game and posterior-mean construction for two arms. Mukerjee, Dasgupta, and Rubin (2018, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 1) supply the arm-labelled setup for general treatment contrasts and unequal replication, with linear unbiased estimation and variance as their target. Bai (2023, Theorems 3.1--3.3) informs the first-order allocation square completion; the new frontier couples its constrained Hessian to the nonregular \(n^{-4/3}\) experiment uniformly over \(n^{-1/6}\) perturbations. Zhao and Ding (2023) and Li and Ding (2017) provide regular multi-arm finite-population asymptotics, not uniform boundary-layer minimax expansions. Levit (1981) and Bickel (1981) inform the spectral and least-favorable-prior route. Aronow and Lopatto (2026, Theorems 1--3) study endpoint minimaxity under design unbiasedness, a restriction not imposed here.
technical_internal_limitation: The value calculation alone is not the finite-experiment theorem. The lower bound fails if the posterior target is scalarized: under the half-effect prior its coefficient is \(b_{A_i}(\alpha)\), and the residual-variance term is needed to obtain \(I(f)+\{2\bar q_1-1/2\}m_1(f)\). The unrestricted prior also needs the vanishing broad component; the pure Airy component has a linear allocation sensitivity. Finally, \(\eta=0\) is a minimizing singular fiber, not a boundary of \(\mathbb R^2\); inserting an \(\eta\)-Laplacian or a transverse boundary condition would define the wrong experiment.
honest_scope: The lossless exact labelled eight-type orbit reduction is imported from the accepted repository parent and is not a contribution of this proposal. The half-wedge tangent program, exact Airy constant, posterior coefficient, uniform Airy upper remainder, allocation-coercive mixture lower bound, sharp \(n^{-1/6}\) frontier, and singular recovery comparison remain statements to prove. The first kill tests are to reproduce the labelled \(n=3\) gap, verify the posterior coefficient including conditional residual variance, and check allocation square completion uniformly over the closed simplex. The proposal does not claim uniqueness of the unrestricted design, equality with fixed-count complete randomization, full Le Cam equivalence of all nuisance experiments, or an endpoint extension beyond binary outcomes. On schedules satisfying \(Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\), the construction must reduce to the published balanced two-arm shifted-binomial experiment.

seed_details.title: Exact three-arm half-wedge Airy constant with the local allocation frontier
seed_details.anchor: SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026, Theorems 2.1--2.3 and 3.1, pages 5--9; MukerjeeDasguptaRubin2018, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 1
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Starting from the inherited exact eight-type orbit likelihood, derive the two-coordinate tangent potential \(V(\theta,\eta)=\max\{|\theta|/2,|\eta|/4\}\) and prove its uniform finite-orbit transfer at the singular fiber.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for the exact three-arm target paired with orbit reduction, Airy minimax analysis, or an allocation frontier found only the two-arm papers and regular multi-arm variance theory.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen because four binary schedule types merely become eight.
seed_details.rebuttal: The inherited eight-type equality does not supply its second-order limit: intersecting face and corner strata, arm-dependent posterior coefficients, and the singular \(\eta=0\) fiber require a new uniform risk bridge and a different spectral normalization.

seed_details.title: Sharp \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation frontier around \(q^\star\)
seed_details.anchor: Bai2023, Theorems 3.1--3.3; SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026, Theorem 3.1; ZhaoDing2023, Sections 2--3
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain the constrained Hessian remainder in the Neyman allocation criterion and couple it uniformly to the nonregular orbit experiment rather than fixing the limiting allocation before the second-order analysis.
seed_details.destination_search: No located paper treats \(n\)-dependent multi-arm allocations at the scale where first-order allocation loss competes with an Airy correction.
seed_details.red_team: The frontier is only a Taylor expansion of the Neyman allocation formula.
seed_details.rebuttal: The Taylor polynomial identifies a candidate penalty but does not prove that the unrestricted nonlinear estimator, labelled likelihood, and least-favorable prior have a uniform \(n^{-4/3}\) expansion along \(q_n=q^\star+O(n^{-1/6})\).

seed_details.title: Contrast-weight phase diagram for three-arm tangent cones
seed_details.anchor: MukerjeeDasguptaRubin2018, Section 2; Bai2023, Theorem 3.2; SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026, Theorem 3.1
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed symmetric contrast by a contrast-indexed support function of the projected eight-type cube and locate changes in its active faces.
seed_details.destination_search: General multi-treatment contrasts are covered by regular variance theory, but no contrast-indexed nonregular minimax phase diagram was located.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine parameterized version of one symmetric contrast.
seed_details.rebuttal: A credible version must prove where the tangent cone and operator domain change and establish both sides of each phase boundary; this is absent from the fixed-contrast calculation.

seed_details.title: Uniform finite-orbit bridge at the singular fiber
seed_details.anchor: Prior proposal exp_boundedcluster_endpoint_orbit_minimax, proof-independence-frontier after equation (41); SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026, Appendix C
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace positive-cell pointwise likelihood convergence by a direct risk comparison that preserves dormant primal constraints and arbitrary posterior versions on disappearing cells.
seed_details.destination_search: The scalar lattice argument in the two-arm paper and classical operator bounds do not treat a rank-degenerate labelled experiment with a measure-valued transverse limit.
seed_details.red_team: Null-cell posterior versions cannot affect risk and hence the boundary is only bookkeeping.
seed_details.rebuttal: A cell null under the limiting prior can remain an active worst-case constraint in the finite primal game, so deleting it can change the minimax envelope at the claimed scale.

seed_details.title: Unrestricted fixed-count complete-randomization constant
seed_details.anchor: Hull2026, Proposition 2 and the conjecture following Theorem 1; SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026, Section 4
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the product Bernoulli likelihood and its discrete Stein identity by the coupled labelled multivariate-hypergeometric orbit while leaving the estimator unrestricted.
seed_details.destination_search: The located strict fixed-count result is affine-class only; no unrestricted three-arm sharp constant was found.
seed_details.red_team: Hull already proves complete randomization is worse.
seed_details.rebuttal: Hull's strict result restricts the estimator class, while his unrestricted theorem optimizes over the design and does not evaluate a fixed-count design.

seed_details.title: Polyhedral Airy constants for every fixed number of arms
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Derive a nonredundant tangent map from \(2^K\) schedule types before invoking a spectral lower bound; a formal multivariate Laplacian has the wrong rank.
seed_details.destination_search: No fixed-\(K\) sharp second-order theorem was located; the available multi-arm results are first-order or regular.
seed_details.red_team: The multivariate Rayleigh-quotient extension is automatic.
seed_details.rebuttal: The orbit polytope, diffusion rank, active domain, and interface conditions must first be derived and change with the contrast; none follows by replacing one derivative with a gradient.

seed_details.title: Finite-\(n\) iid-optimality and label-gap classification
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Eliminate the abstract primal and dual variables from the arm-labelled complementary-slackness system to obtain a symbolic active-set criterion.
seed_details.destination_search: The prior finite game proves existence but stops before classification, and the published convex program is two-arm.
seed_details.red_team: This merely solves a finite convex program separately for each \(n\).
seed_details.rebuttal: The contribution would be a necessary-and-sufficient symbolic classification and proof of the first label gap, not numerical optimization.

seed_details.title: Critical prognostic-strength frontier for independent versus stratified assignment
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Intersect the endpoint cube with a within-stratum dispersion restriction, which destroys the separability of the endpoint adversary.
seed_details.destination_search: Existing stratification results impose prognostic structure or fix conventional estimators; none jointly optimizes unrestricted nonlinear estimators over bounded schedules.
seed_details.red_team: Bai and Kallus already show informative stratification is optimal.
seed_details.rebuttal: Those results do not derive the critical transition against independent allocation in the bounded fixed-schedule unrestricted-estimator game.

seed_details.title: Exact weak-null inversion for the nonlinear three-arm minimax rule
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace sharp-null imputation by maximization over compatible eight-type counts under a weak finite-population contrast null.
seed_details.destination_search: No exact weak-null inversion based on the three-arm minimax orbit rule was located.
seed_details.red_team: Invert the usual Fisher randomization test.
seed_details.rebuttal: The target is a weak null with unidentified complete schedules, so sharp-null imputation is unavailable and nuisance maximization is load-bearing.

seed_details.title: Endpoint reduction for bounded three-arm outcomes
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Apply coordinatewise endpoint Bernoulliization and conditional expectation to the multi-arm observation map.
seed_details.destination_search: The two-arm endpoint contraction is explicit in both anchors; no concrete obstruction to extending the same argument across a finite arm set was found.
seed_details.red_team: The binary subclass gives one inequality and conditional endpoint randomization gives the other verbatim.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds absent a finite-\(n\) labelled counterexample.

literature_map.settled: For two bounded-outcome arms, unrestricted joint design and estimation reduce to a scalar endpoint game attained by iid half assignment; the binary value has the Airy \(n^{-4/3}\) expansion.
literature_map.unsettled: Neither paper treats three arms, eight labelled response types, a face/corner experiment, or local allocation perturbations.

literature_map.settled: General arm-labelled contrasts, unequal replications, finite-population variance bookkeeping, and regular fixed-allocation asymptotics are available.
literature_map.unsettled: These results do not optimize over nonlinear estimators and arbitrary designs or resolve a nonregular second-order minimax boundary layer.

literature_map.settled: Permutation symmetrization and quadratic allocation criteria yield finite-sample optimality results in restricted linear or design-unbiased problems.
literature_map.unsettled: The \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation scale and its interaction with nonlinear shrinkage are absent.

literature_map.settled: One-dimensional second-order minimax constants can be obtained from square completion, least-favorable priors, and a positive ground state.
literature_map.unsettled: No cited result justifies the degenerate direct-integral limit, the coalesced \(\eta=0\) interface, or a measure-valued transverse dual.

literature_map.settled: The lossless exact labelled eight-type orbit-game reduction, finite saddle, and complementary-slackness bookkeeping including zero-likelihood cells are imported infrastructure.
literature_map.unsettled: The parent does not derive the half-wedge Airy constant, prove a uniform bridge at \(\eta=0\), or characterize the \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation frontier.

literature_checklist.author: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 2.2 and 3.1 prove the unrestricted two-arm reduction and \(n^{-4/3}\) Airy expansion; Appendix C supplies the lattice upper and lower constructions.

literature_checklist.author: Hull
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 1 gives an exact unrestricted two-arm endpoint game and nonlinear attaining estimator, while unrestricted fixed-count strictness remains conjectural.

literature_checklist.author: Bai
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 3.1--3.3 use permutation symmetrization and quadratic optimization for linear estimation; the displayed Neyman formula is two-arm.

literature_checklist.author: Mukerjee, Dasgupta, and Rubin
literature_checklist.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
literature_checklist.one_line: Sections 2--3 and Theorem 1 give arm-labelled finite-population contrast and assignment-probability bookkeeping for general treatments.

literature_checklist.author: Zhao and Ding
literature_checklist.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper develops regular design-based multi-arm regression asymptotics under fixed positive allocation limits, not a local minimax frontier.

literature_checklist.author: Li and Ding
literature_checklist.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems for multi-treatment complete randomization provide combinatorial central limits but not \(n^{-4/3}\) uniform risk expansions.

literature_checklist.author: Levit
literature_checklist.venue: Theory of Probability and Its Applications
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper develops second-order asymptotic minimax analysis through a problem-specific differential operator.

literature_checklist.author: Bickel
literature_checklist.one_line: Restricted normal-mean minimax analysis provides a classical least-favorable-prior and boundary-layer comparator.

literature_checklist.author: Aronow and Lopatto
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 1--3 characterize endpoint minimax risk and pairwise-independent sampling under design unbiasedness, a distinct restriction.
